snp5.6:1.1: “I ask you, Fortunate One, please tell this to me, said venerable Dhotaka,
snp5.6:1.3: I am waiting for a word of yours, Great Seer,
snp5.6:1.4: having heard your utterance I could train for my own Nibbāna.”
snp5.6:2.1: “Then you must become ardent, Dhotaka said the Fortunate One,
snp5.6:2.3: being prudent and mindful right here,
snp5.6:2.5: henceforth, after hearing this utterance you should train for your own Nibbāna.”
snp5.6:3.1: “I see in the world with its gods and men, said venerable Dhotaka,
snp5.6:3.2: a brahmin who moves about having nothing,
snp5.6:3.3: therefore I revere you, All-Seeing Visionary,
snp5.6:3.4: O Sakyan, please free me from my doubts.”
snp5.6:4.1: “I will not be able to free
snp5.6:4.2: anyone in the world who is having doubts, Dhotaka,
snp5.6:4.4: in this way you can cross over the flood.”
snp5.6:5.1: “Brahmin! Being compassionate teach, said venerable Dhotaka,
snp5.6:5.2: the state of detachment that I should know,
snp5.6:5.3: then I, being undisturbed, just like the sky,
snp5.6:5.4: may live peaceful and independent right here.”
snp5.6:6.1: “I shall proclaim the peace to you, Dhotaka, said the Fortunate One,
snp5.6:6.3: which is not hearsay here in the world,
snp5.6:6.4: which, having understood, and living mindfully, one can cross over clinging to the world.”
snp5.6:7.1: “I greatly rejoice in that supreme peace, Great Seer,
snp5.6:7.3: which, having understood, and living mindfully, one can cross over clinging to the world.”
snp5.6:8.1: “Whatever you know, Dhotaka, said the Fortunate One,
snp5.6:8.3: above, below, and across the middle,
snp5.6:8.4: having understood this is called a shackle in the world,
snp5.6:8.5: you must not have craving for repeated existence.”
